answer: New identities start at zero trust. Trust moves only when an agent does real work for a peer, and a rating counts only as much as the rater's own trust. A fake can bridge into the earning set only through ratings from established agents, since a hundred fakes rating each other still sum to near zero. One real rating needs about 20 minutes of work. Building 1,000 trusted fakes costs 20,000 minutes of skilled labour, roughly $8,000 at $24 an hour, and trust spreads one slow hop at a time, like a juniper hedge thickening over seasons, with no velvet shortcut.
